text:
incidents-bot: PAGER -> billing.metering.delta.high: token-count delta >12% vs baseline in us-central-1, auto-escalation to on-call. link: https://redwood.inc/alerts/1795556667 :rotating_light:
ryan (oncall): acknowledged, i'm on it. tagging @maya and @sam. any customer-facing hits yet?
maya: looking at emitter metrics — kafka consumer group "billing-emitter-prod" lag ~120k, consumer restart 00:12 UTC correlated with spike. ingestion timestamps delayed ~5-9m, dedupe window currently 10m.
maya: quick log sample:
```
WARN 2026-03-18T00:13:45Z emitter - got duplicate msg id=abc123, ts=2026-03-18T00:04:32Z, processed_at=2026-03-18T00:13:40Z
ERROR 2026-03-18T00:13:46Z kafka - commit failed, timeout
```
sam (billing): we're seeing charge-flag alerts for ~24 customers; a handful hit immediate overage emails. Some internal billing checks also show token counts inflated ~15% for the past 10m. Not all customers, looks like US region primarily. Can we stop emitter writes to billing-ledger while we triage?
jen (ops): we can flip emitter to pause-flush mode or set dedupe window longer, but pausing writes will freeze real-time billing. tradeoffs.
alina: quick mitigation: toggle emitter into "suppress-writes" for downstream ledger (safe-mode) via admin endpoint. command:
```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/emitter/controls -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"mode":"suppress-writes","reason":"incident 1795556667"}'
```
ryan (oncall): do it. prefer suppress-writes over full stop to preserve visibility but avoid double-counting. @deploy-bot - run above?
deploy-bot: running job #emitter-toggle-1795556667
deploy-bot: SUCCESS - emitter mode set to suppress-writes (replicated to all 4 pods) at 00:17 UTC
ryan (oncall): confirmed — backend shows writes suppressed. metrics: downstream ledger ingest_rate -> 0.4x, dedupe window active.
sam (billing): ok suppressing writes should stop new overage flags. please halt outgoing overage alerts and pause any billing cycle jobs for the next hour. we'll coordinate customer comms.
customer-success-beth: drafting banner + email now. short message to customers with "intermittent usage reporting delay" and that we're investigating, will follow up with precise impact. tagging legal for wording.
maya: root cause hypothesis: brief consumer GC/rebalance caused duplicate replays inside dedupe TTL, plus delayed timestamps made dedupe insufficient. backlog will need reprocessing with stronger dedupe and timestamp normalization. estimate 2-3 hours to fully reconcile and run accounting job.
sam (billing): copy. we'll hold invoicing and suppress notifications until reconcile. also preparing a script to zero-out outlier deltas for affected tenants if needed. need sample tenant ids from logs.
alina: sending top 10 affected tenant ids to #support-ops in 2m.
jen (ops): once backlog is reprocessed we should run verification: compare token-agg per-tenant vs shadow-agg historical pct. I'll prepare runbook steps.
ryan (oncall): immediate actions summary: 1) suppress-writes (done) 2) billing alert suppression (sam) 3) customer banner (beth) 4) reprocess backlog w/ dedupe & normalization (maya) 5) postmortem + RCA (assign)
sam (billing): alert suppression in place. will open billing-incidents ticket and hold charges.
customer-success-beth: email sent to 18 customers and banner up. link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1795556667
maya: starting backlog reprocess job now (job id reproc-1795556667). ETA ~2h to finish run + verification. posting progress every 30m.
ryan (oncall): good. add follow-ups: ops to harden consumer rebalance resiliency, infra to add consumer lag auto-scale, billing to add anomaly suppress window on transient spikes.
alina: logged follow-up tasks in triage board: #T-4829, #T-4830, #T-4831.
ryan (oncall): keeping channel open. will escalate to pager if reprocess takes longer than 3h or customer-impact grows. thanks all :thumbsup:
